registered_by: executor seat, on E08-shot, before the first submission of any E08 graph
how_these_were_chosen: The date as a plain integer with a run index appended, continuing the rule specs/E09-seeds.json and specs/E09-A3-seeds.json use: 2026-08-12 runs 11, 12 and 13. The property that matters is that every number is fixed BEFORE any result is seen, and a date-derived seed is checkable against this file's own git timestamp. No seed here was drawn from a prior run, from any served template, or from anything this seat had already looked at.

allocation.2026081211: the probe — the one generation this wave authorises up front
allocation.2026081212: reserve 1, spendable only on a named cause the probe surfaces

why_the_index_starts_at_11_rather_than_0: specs/E09-A3-seeds.json already registered 2026081201 and 2026081202 on the same calendar day, and both were spent or reserved against the E09 clean-chain trajectory. Reusing either number here would put a seed registered for one experiment onto another, and the record would afterwards have to explain which run a number belonged to. The offset keeps every seed on this rig traceable to exactly one registration.

ceiling.note: 3 generations in wave 1 — 1 probe plus 2 reserve. Gate C arms on the measured billing number from estimate_credits, recorded before the first submission, and halts before any submission that would exceed the ceiling. Spent credits have no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
ceiling.why_machine_readable: The value was free prose and no tool under tools/ read the key, while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated. CLAUDE.md makes the credit ceiling a per-spec obligation and records that spent credits have no compensator, so the one unrecoverable resource in this repo was bounded by a string nothing could parse. The prose is not deleted: it is `note`, verbatim, and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it. CORRECTION, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 8, F-6c5c537b). This paragraph used to argue the fix with the clause “while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated”, and to close “and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it”. Both halves were measured on the tree and only one survived. `grep -rn allocation tools/ --include=*.py` returns 0 hits: `allocation` has no reader at all, so it is exactly as unread as `ceiling` was when it was filed. `seeds` has seven readers — build_animate_payload.py:484 (main), build_camera_i2v_payload.py:1164 (main), build_i2v_payload.py:767 (main), build_lora_arm_payload.py:466 (gate_s), build_r2v_payload.py:302 (build_and_write), build_t2v_payload.py:498 (main) and gate_saved_graph.py:695 (main) — each handing the list to a seed gate, so that half of the claim holds. And no tool reads `ceiling` from a seeds spec either: every `ceiling` hit under tools/ is `armature_core.assembly`'s unrelated CASCADE slot ceiling, or a builder passing that one. So `ceiling.submissions` is a number a submission step COULD count against and none does today — the bound is held by the spec and the executor, not by code. The original claim is kept above rather than deleted, because the correction is more useful than the original. tests/test_seeds_specs.py pins the measurement; the day a builder counts against `ceiling.submissions`, that test flips with it and this paragraph is rewritten again. RE-ANCHORED, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 14). Three of the seven citations moved because gates were added above their readers, and the line numbers were RE-MEASURED rather than re-typed: build_i2v_payload.py 620 -> 687 (start_image_record gained the fit_disagrees_with_the_file andon, F-e17613c2), build_r2v_payload.py 217 -> 272 (Gate CEILING gained its behaviour-keyed hosted-node census, F-eec3f145), and gate_saved_graph.py 487 -> 602 (route_facts reads the two facts Gate ROUTE needs off the builder's payload record, F-2da88c51). The other four are unmoved. The function name beside each number is the anchor that survives the next move; tests/test_seeds_specs.py checks the pair, which is how this drift was found. RE-ANCHORED, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 16, F-0682bd00). All seven citations moved, and the thing they cite changed with them: every one of the seven sites was a bare `json.load(fh)["seeds"]` index (or, in build_lora_arm_payload, the disarming `registry.get("seeds") or []`), and all seven now call ONE reader, `build_assembly_payload.read_seed_registration`, which refuses a missing file, unreadable JSON, a non-mapping document, a missing `seeds` key and a non-list `seeds` by name. The line numbers were RE-MEASURED, never re-typed: build_animate_payload.py 482 -> 484, build_camera_i2v_payload.py 1110 -> 1164, build_i2v_payload.py 687 -> 767, build_lora_arm_payload.py 463 -> 466, build_r2v_payload.py 272 -> 302, build_t2v_payload.py 496 -> 498, gate_saved_graph.py 602 -> 695. `build_t2v_payload` also gained the `no_seed_and_no_registration` clause its three sibling builders already carried before their own `sorted(registry)[0]`: an empty registration used to reach the operator as `IndexError: list index out of range` at exit 1, the code that module's own halt block reserves for a crash. The seven remain seven, and the eight specs remain eight copies of one paragraph.

binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/gates.py::gate_s_seed_registration enforces both clauses at build time and tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces them again against the graph that is about to run.
